source_refs.note: Exercise 5.1 (book p. 154), Question 9; answer key PDF 306 (Answers 5.1, key numbered 11).

blocks.prompt: 9 (i) Find the family of lines through the point of intersection of the lines \(2x - 3y + 5 = 0\), \(x + 4y - 7 = 0\). Find the member of the family which is parallel to \(y = 2x + 1\).
blocks.explanation:
Family of lines through the point of intersection: \(\ell_1 + k\ell_2 = 0\).
The member we want must also satisfy one slope condition: parallel to \(y = 2x + 1\) (slope \(2\)).
Plan: family, its slope in terms of \(k\), the slope condition gives \(k\), substitute back.
steps:
Given: \(2x - 3y + 5 = 0\) and \(x + 4y - 7 = 0\).
To find: the family through their point of intersection, and its member which is parallel to \(y = 2x + 1\) (slope \(2\)).
Method: \(\ell_1 + k\ell_2 = 0\) (Section 5.5, Example 11), then a slope condition.

The family
\[2x - 3y + 5 + k(x + 4y - 7) = 0\]
\[(2 + k)x + (-3 + 4k)y + (5 - 7k) = 0\]
Why: every line \(\ell_1 + k\ell_2 = 0\) passes through the meeting point; collect the \(x\), \(y\) and constant terms. (The answer key writes \(\lambda\) for \(k\).)

Slope of the family
\[m = -\dfrac{2 + k}{4k - 3}\]
Why: the slope of \(ax + by + c = 0\) is \(-\frac{a}{b}\).

Use the condition
\[-\dfrac{2 + k}{4k - 3} = 2\]
\[-2 - k = 8k - 6\]
\[9k = 4\]
\[k = \dfrac{4}{9}\]
Why: parallel lines have equal slopes; cross-multiply to get a simple equation in \(k\).

Substitute \(k = \frac{4}{9}\) in the family
\[\tfrac{22}{9}x + \left(-3 + \tfrac{16}{9}\right)y + \left(5 - \tfrac{28}{9}\right) = 0\]
\[\tfrac{22}{9}x - \tfrac{11}{9}y + \tfrac{17}{9} = 0\]
\[22x - 11y + 17 = 0\]
Why: put \(k\) in each coefficient, then clear fractions.

Check:
Slope \(\frac{22}{11} = 2\). The given lines meet at \(\left(\frac{1}{11}, \frac{19}{11}\right)\), and \(22\left(\frac{1}{11}\right) - 11\left(\frac{19}{11}\right) + 17 = 2 - 19 + 17 = 0\). Matches answer key 11(i).

blocks.prompt: 9 (ii) Find the family of lines through the point of intersection of the lines \(2x - 3y + 5 = 0\), \(x + 4y - 7 = 0\). Find the member of the family which is perpendicular to \(y = x\).
blocks.explanation:
Family of lines through the point of intersection: \(\ell_1 + k\ell_2 = 0\).
The member we want must also satisfy one slope condition: perpendicular to \(y = x\) (slope \(1\), so we need slope \(-1\)).
Plan: family, its slope in terms of \(k\), the slope condition gives \(k\), substitute back.
steps:
Given: \(2x - 3y + 5 = 0\) and \(x + 4y - 7 = 0\).
To find: the family through their point of intersection, and its member which is perpendicular to \(y = x\) (slope \(1\), so we need slope \(-1\)).
Method: \(\ell_1 + k\ell_2 = 0\) (Section 5.5, Example 11), then a slope condition.

The family
\[2x - 3y + 5 + k(x + 4y - 7) = 0\]
\[(2 + k)x + (-3 + 4k)y + (5 - 7k) = 0\]
Why: every line \(\ell_1 + k\ell_2 = 0\) passes through the meeting point; collect the \(x\), \(y\) and constant terms. (The answer key writes \(\lambda\) for \(k\).)

Slope of the family
\[m = -\dfrac{2 + k}{4k - 3}\]
Why: the slope of \(ax + by + c = 0\) is \(-\frac{a}{b}\).

Use the condition
\[-\dfrac{2 + k}{4k - 3} \times 1 = -1\]
\[2 + k = 4k - 3\]
\[3k = 5\]
\[k = \dfrac{5}{3}\]
Why: perpendicular lines have \(m_1m_2 = -1\); cross-multiply to get a simple equation in \(k\).

Substitute \(k = \frac{5}{3}\) in the family
\[\tfrac{11}{3}x + \left(-3 + \tfrac{20}{3}\right)y + \left(5 - \tfrac{35}{3}\right) = 0\]
\[\tfrac{11}{3}x + \tfrac{11}{3}y - \tfrac{20}{3} = 0\]
\[11x + 11y - 20 = 0\]
Why: put \(k\) in each coefficient, then clear fractions.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key (Answers 5.1, number 11 (ii)) prints \(11x - 11y + 20 = 0\). That line has slope \(+1\), so it is parallel to \(y = x\), not perpendicular, and it misses the point of intersection: \(11\left(\frac{1}{11}\right) - 11\left(\frac{19}{11}\right) + 20 = 2 \ne 0\). The correct answer is \(11x + 11y - 20 = 0\).
